newsitem.title: USA: Ex-fugitive's rape retrial set to begin in U.S..
newsitem.headline: Ex-fugitive's rape retrial set to begin in U.S..

text.p: The retrial of accused rapist Alex Kelly, who fled the United States and lived as a fugitive for eight years before surrendering in Switzerland in 1995, is set to begin Thursday, lawyers in the case said.
Kelly's first trial in the 1986 alleged rape of a 16-year-old neighbour in Darien, Connecticut, ended in a hung jury in November 1996.
The retrial was delayed by weeks of legal wrangling and a lengthy jury-selection process.
Kelly, 30, was free on $1 million bond -- secured by his parents' house and other properties in Darien -- while awaiting retrial.
Earlier this year he requested and received Irish citizenship. The move riled prosecutors, who said they were worried about an increased risk that he would flee the country again.
A former high school wrestling star, Kelly was accused in February 1986 of raping a 16-year-old girl and a 17-year-old girl in separate incidents.
He fled the United State on the eve of his first scheduled trial in 1987, embarking on an eight-year odyssey through 15 countries that included time on the ski slopes of Europe.
The authorities have said his European travels were financed by his wealthy parents.
He surrendered early in 1995 as federal authorities were closing in on him.
The alleged rapes are being tried separately. No date has been set for the second case.
Kelly's accuser is now a 27-year-old professional. His defence lawyers say the sex was consensual.
Kelly's first trial ended in a mistrial last year after the jury deadlocked 4-2 in favour of a guilty verdict. In Connecticut guilty verdicts must be unanimous.
The retrial will be presided over by a different Stamford superior court judge, Kevin Tierney.
The trial is expected to take about three weeks.
